data.long_meaning: To believe in something with strong conviction and certainty. The name Faih carries the meaning “Trust, Faith” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Faih usually hope their child will grow to embody trust, faith and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Faih total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Faith" in Islamic culture represents unwavering trust and reliance in Allah (God). It is a reminder of the importance of maintaining a strong connection with the Divine and trusting in His guidance and protection. In the Islamic context, having faith is not just belief, but rather a way of living one's life in accordance with the teachings of the Quran and the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is also an essential component of the Islamic belief system, as it forms the foundation for ethical behavior, moral values, and a fulfilling spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Faith" signifies a bond or relationship between the believer and Allah. It represents a deep sense of commitment, trust, and devotion to the Divine Creator, who is believed to be the source of all knowledge, power, and wisdom. By having faith, one is able to connect with the divine force and tap into the limitless storehouse of blessings and mercy. It allows the believer to overcome obstacles, find inner peace, and achieve lasting happiness and contentment in life. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said, "Faith consists of fifteen things: to believe in Allah and His Messenger, to perform prayer, to pay the zakat, to fast during the month of Ramadan, to make the pilgrimage to Mecca, to believe in the Day of Judgment, to speak the truth, to forbear from lying, to respect the ties of kinship, to be kind to neighbors, to keep promises, to be friends only for truth, and to abhor what is disgraceful." (Bukhari and Muslim). Embracing these principles and practicing them consistently can lead to a deep sense of peace, tranquility, and a strong sense of purpose in life.
